reviewed_finding: The source claims are PROVED_LEAN, but wdp_growth_subcomplex_monotone is the monotonicity of a List Nat sum under appending, and wdp_two_simplex_attachment_preserves_phi1 is rfl because attachTwoSimplex updates only the triangle list; neither involves the minimum over potentials that defines Phi1. The Rust witness uses hard-coded constants. The real content is proved here: restriction monotonicity of the attained weighted-L1 minimum under hypotheses the source does not state (d0 compatibility, h restricted, weights not raised, minima attained), with kernel counterexamples when a hypothesis is dropped, the definitional invariance of Phi1 under attachment, the additive rise of the representative norm and gamma2_repair (equal to the source Gamma2 at the minimal residual when d1 d0 = 0). The necessity wording of the source (a decrease requires deleted cells, changed weights or changed values) is the contrapositive of phi_growth_not_lower for the modelled structure. Source external hashes match the pins (Obstruction.lean, derivation_dag_witnesses.rs, DerivationDagQMClosure.lean); the paper pin tfq_0346 is a CRLF-era hash.

claim_boundary.supports: Kernel-checked over finite index types, for rational windows whose attained minima Phi1 exist (existence of minimisers is a hypothesis, IsPhi, not proved): if the sub-window d0 is the restriction of the big d0 (hcompat), its cochain is the restriction and its weights are at most the restrictions of the big weights, then Phi1(sub) <= Phi1(big) (phi_restrict_le); hence growth with an extending cochain and weights not lowered never lowers Phi1 (phi_growth_not_lower, which is the contrapositive of the source necessity wording: a decrease needs deleted cells, lowered weights, an incompatible d0 or changed cochain values); Phi1 <= the unrepaired residual sum; attaching a 2-cell leaves (D0, w, h) and hence Phi1 untouched (definitional) and adds |row . h| to the representative norm ||d1 h||_1; this is the source Gamma2 (the norm at the minimal residual) only when d1 d0 = 0, which gamma2_repair proves and which every valid row preserves (closed_attach, triangle_row_closed). Boundaries as kernel instances: incompatible d0, weights raised 2 -> 3 (Phi1 4 -> 6), and norm arithmetic only for J(a,b) = |a+b| + |a-b|/4 with J(1,-1) = 1/2 < J(1,0) = 5/4 (for d0 = 0 the defect of h is J(h), so deleting a coordinate raises it; this consequence is not stated as a theorem about Phi1). Native table of 82 pairs (9 named restrictions plus all 63 edge subsets of K4 for one cochain, 6 attachments incl. an invalid row, 4 edits) with a verified primal potential and dual vector for both windows of every pair and Phi1 recomputed by the dual LP in the checker; the strict decreases from deleting cells (3 -> 0), lowering weights (6 -> 2) and changing the cochain (1 -> 0) are native rows, not kernel instances.
claim_boundary.does_not_support: Monotonicity for arbitrary norms J or renormalised weights (the instances show it fails), or when the sub d0 is not the restriction of d0; existence of minimisers for weighted L1 as a Lean theorem; that each of the three failing hypotheses is by itself sufficient to lower Phi1 in general (kernel instances exist for raised weights and a changed d0; the native rows cover deletion, a changed cochain and lowered weights); equal-weight subdivision and filtration limit pages (clauses of WDP-CH04-P09 absent from the source Lean); the source Gamma2 at a minimal residual of a non-closed window (non-unique, withheld); complex coefficients; any physical reading.
claim_boundary.narrowest_claim: For weighted-L1 graph windows with attained minima, restricting to a sub-window whose d0, cochain and weights are the restrictions (weights at most the restrictions of the big weights) never raises Phi1, and attaching 2-cells with d1 d0 = 0 leaves Phi1 unchanged and cannot lower Gamma2; in the native table, deleting cells, lowering weights and changing the cochain strictly lowered Phi1 (kernel instances exist only for raised weights and a changed d0).
claim_boundary.next_test: Prove the equal-weight subdivision clause of WDP-CH04-P09 (subdividing an edge through a new degree-two vertex with equal weights leaves Phi1 unchanged) as a Lean theorem over IsPhi and check it by exact enumeration; separately discharge the existence of minimisers (IsPhi attainment) for weighted L1 so that phi_restrict_le has no attained-minimum hypothesis.

additional_scope_clarifications.reviewed_target_qualification: Restriction monotonicity of Phi1 holds for a weighted-L1 norm with the sub d0, cochain and weights the restrictions (weights not raised); the source Lean theorems prove only a List Nat sum bound and an rfl, and the statement fails for re-normalised weights or a norm not monotone under coordinate deletion.
additional_scope_clarifications.historical_target_status: Original target retained verbatim as source history; the corrected narrow scope governs this run.

second_review.notes: Cold read of run 20261021T175809Z_staged; I also recompiled WdpGrowthNoRepair.lean (exit 0, axioms propext / Classical.choice / Quot.sound only). phi_restrict_le is a sound proof: hcompat (D' restricted along eps and iota), hh, hw (w' <= w o eps), hw0 (w >= 0), both minima attained; step1 restricts the optimal big potential, step2 drops the non-negative terms outside the image of the injective eps. phi_growth_not_lower is its contrapositive (so the necessity half of N02 is proved for the modelled structure, and the profile no longer lists it as open). phi_attach_iff is Iff.rfl, gamma2_attach / gamma2_attach_ge hold for every row, closed_attach / triangle_row_closed / gamma2_repair carry the d1 d0 = 0 link to the source Gamma2; the three boundary instances check by hand (Phi1 4 -> 6 for weights 2 -> 3 on the first two parallel edges; d0 = (1) vs (0) gives 0 vs 1; J(1,-1) = 1/2 < J(1,0) = 5/4 with the three norm axioms). The profile states that nonmonotone_norm_instance is norm arithmetic only and that the Phi1 consequence is not a theorem. Checker: Phi1 of both windows by dual-LP vertex enumeration, each window's primal potential and dual vector verified exactly (weak-duality certificate, so the Phi1 values do not depend on the enumeration being complete), window B rebuilt from the operation by a different decomposition, public windows validated, ids fixed to the 82 declared pairs, and the 63 K4 subsets counted unconditionally. I read public_input.json: the 63 k4_sub_NN cases have keep-lists equal to the bits of NN and one shared base window, so 'all 63 edge subsets' is true of the actual input. Earlier pass (a): all seven amendments are in the final text (IsPhi attainment hypothesis, d1 d0 = 0 qualifier for Gamma2, J-norm wording as arithmetic only, 'weights at most the restrictions', native-table attribution of the strict decreases, does_not_support and next_test rewritten, NoRule -> NotAWindow); (b) no weakening in the rebuild; new mutants cover Gamma2 for a non-window, lowered weights called raising, deletion called neutral, routing name as class, a K4 subset raised, and a non-optimal witness; (c) residual issues: (1) the checker enforces the 82-pair family only by id (EXPECTED_IDS) plus validate_case; it does not re-derive that k4_sub_NN keeps the edges given by the bits of NN. The stage packet digest binds the public input, so this is not exploitable in this run, but the '63 subsets' evidence rests on the input generator, not on the checker. (2) does_not_support says the equal-weight subdivision AND filtration-limit-page clauses are 'clauses of WDP-CH04-P09'; in the ledger P09 contains the subdivision clause and N02 contains the filtration-limit clause. (3) The Lean theorems are for arbitrary rational matrices D over finite index types, not graph windows; the graph-specific content (triangle_row_closed) is the only graph lemma, so 'weighted-L1 graph windows' in narrowest_claim is narrower than what is proved, which is safe. (4) The attained-minimum hypothesis is the real open item for the Lean side; for graph windows with rational weights the minimum is attained (finite LP), but that is not proved in Lean and the checker only certifies attainment on the 82 windows. (5) Mutants are single-record edits; the incompatible-d0 and non-monotone-norm boundaries have no native pair and no mutant (Lean only), which is acceptable because they are labelled kernel instances.

dag_suggestion.statement: For weighted-L1 windows with attained minima: if the sub-window's d0 is the restriction of the big d0, its cochain is the restriction and its weights are at most the restrictions, then Phi1(sub) <= Phi1(big), so growth with an extending cochain and weights not lowered never lowers Phi1 (a decrease needs deleting cells, lowered weights, a changed d0 or changed cochain values); attaching a 2-cell whose row satisfies d1 d0 = 0 leaves (D0, w, h) and hence Phi1 unchanged (definitional) and adds |row . h| to Gamma2 = ||d1 h||_1, so Gamma2 cannot decrease. Monotonicity fails when weights are raised, when d0 is not the restriction, or for a norm not monotone under coordinate deletion (norm arithmetic only). Equal-weight subdivision, filtration limit pages, complex coefficients and the existence of minimisers are not covered.
dag_suggestion.bottleneck: The source Lean theorems (wdp_growth_subcomplex_monotone, wdp_two_simplex_attachment_preserves_phi1) are a List Nat sum bound and an rfl; the real statement is proved here only under hcompat, restricted cochain, weights not raised and attained minima; equal-weight subdivision and existence of minimisers are unported.

earlier_pass.notes: The mathematical core is correct and the right fix to the vacuous source theorems: phi_restrict_le (hcompat for all x, cochain restriction, w' <= w, w >= 0, both minima attained) is a sound proof, phi_attach_iff is Iff.rfl because IsPhi takes (D0, w, h) only, gamma2_attach / triangle_row_closed are correct (the sum_ite_eq' reduction holds even for coinciding edges), and the three boundary instances check by hand (4 vs 6; J(1,-1)=1/2, J(1,0)=5/4; D=1 vs D=0). The checker computes Phi1 by dual-LP vertex enumeration against a primal producer, rebuilds window B by a different decomposition, and the 19 pairs (9/6/4) are as stated. Problems. (1) Gamma2 convention: Win.gamma2 and the checker use the norm of d1 h at the given representative, whereas the source (run.rs 169-171: 'Gamma2 = ||d1 h1*||_1 on the SAME minimal residual') uses the minimal residual; the two agree only when d1 d0 = 0 (this is gamma2_repair in the sibling quotient module). gamma2_attach and gamma2_attach_ge hold for every row, with no closure hypothesis, so supports 'adds |row . h| to Gamma2' is a statement about the representative norm; narrowest_claim has the qualifier 'with d1 d0 = 0', supports does not, and no theorem ties Gamma2 to the minimiser. The invalid-row pair (tri_attach_invalid_row, Gamma2_b = 1) reports a number the source would not call Gamma2 (non-closed windows have non-unique L1 minimisers, which is why the source says SAME residual). (2) IsPhi existence: every inequality is conditional on attained minima (hp, hq); the Lean docstring says so but the claim boundary does not. (3) nonmonotone_norm_instance states only values of Jn and the norm axioms; no window, IsPhi or restriction occurs in it (IsPhi is weighted-L1 specific), so 'a norm J ... not monotone under coordinate deletion' is a fact about J, and its consequence for Phi1 (with d0 = 0 the defect is J(h); 'restriction' of (1,-1) read as the zero-padded (1,0)) is docstring only. (4) narrowest_claim 'whereas deleting cells, lowering weights or changing the cochain can lower it': the kernel instances all run in the other direction (hypothesis dropped => Phi1 goes up from big to sub, i.e. down from sub to big for weights and d0); there is no kernel instance for a changed cochain or for a strictly smaller Phi1 after deleting cells. Those facts are native-table rows (k4_restrict_one_edge 3 -> 0; tri_edit_w_down 6 -> 2; tri_edit_h_to_exact 1 -> 0) and should be attributed as such. (5) The necessity half is mis-described as open: the source (TFQ-0346, N02) says a decrease 'requires deleting cells, changing declared weights, or changing existing edge values', and phi_growth_not_lower is exactly the contrapositive of that for the modelled structure: with hcompat, restricted cochain and weights not lowered, Phi1 cannot drop in growing. So does_not_support ('only the three sufficient routes are tabulated, not necessity') and next_test ('Prove or refute the converse half ... a strict decrease forces ...') restate something that is already proved, up to attained minima. What is genuinely unpaid in the same source clause is the equal-weight subdivision statement of P09 and existence of minimisers in Lean. (6) Field diag_b = 'NoRule' for a non-window is a routing/status name placed in the diagnostic-class field, the axis confusion PG-WDP-DIAGNOSTIC-NOT-ROUTING exists to prevent; use a neutral marker. Checker: positive points as above; weaknesses are that nothing validates the public windows (weights positive, endpoints in range, cochain ints, base window closed), the exhaustive K4 subset test claimed in relation_evidence lives in the Python unit test and is not part of the certificate or checker, and the theorem-level checks collapse to the verdict recomputation. Mutants are genuine misreadings (rescaled weights called monotone, attachment lowers Phi1, residual sum read as Phi1, gauge shift read as repair) but all are single-record edits; no mutant uses Gamma2 at the minimiser versus the representative, and no native pair exercises the incompatible-d0 or non-monotone-norm boundary (Lean only).
